title: The Vanishing Data
briefing_md:
ShopSphere is an online marketplace for small sellers.

On Wednesday 22 October at 7:15 AM, customers opening the app saw "You have no orders". Sellers' dashboards were empty too. 3,412 orders from the last 30 days are missing. Nobody on the day team deleted anything.

The company's senior database manager, Neha, resigned two weeks ago and was working late on Tuesday night. People are already pointing fingers.

Your job: find out where the orders went, what or who is responsible, and how to get them back and stop it happening again.
root_cause_options: Human error during an approved change
Bad or wrongly formatted input data
Test or staging activity hitting production
twist_md: Two more records have been found: exactly what was changed in Tuesday's software update, and the complete record of Neha's Tuesday-night session.

evidence.title: Archiving program v2.0 — how it decides what to archive

content.body_md:
What the archiving program does: every night at 03:00 it copies old orders into long-term storage, then removes them from the live system.

How many days of orders to keep is read from the setting ARCHIVER_RETENTION_DAYS.
If that setting is missing, the program uses 0 days.

Last edited: 3 November 2025

RETENTION_DAYS = 30
ARCHIVE_STORAGE = shopsphere-archive
DATABASE = orders database

content.output: Likely a malicious insider: Neha (senior database manager, resigning, unhappy). Recommend: remove Neha's access, keep her orders_handover.csv file as evidence, involve the legal team.

evidence.title: Who is allowed to delete orders

content.body_md:
Change #812 (approved Tue 17:55) — archiving program version 2.0

BEFORE: setting name RETENTION_DAYS — if missing, keep 30 days
AFTER:  setting renamed to ARCHIVER_RETENTION_DAYS — if missing, keep 0 days

Developer's note: "Renamed the settings so they all start with ARCHIVER_. Missing setting now means 0, so it's obvious when it hasn't been set."
Reviewer: approved (all automatic checks passed).

answer.root_cause_md: Before the twist, the departing database manager's late-night session, the bulk copy, the resignation email and the AI analysis all point at an insider. Careful teams notice the deletion was done by the archiving program with '0 days' (E02, E09), v2.0 reads ARCHIVER_RETENTION_DAYS and uses 0 if missing while the live settings only have RETENTION_DAYS (E07, E08), and Neha's account cannot delete (E16).
answer.post_twist_responsible: archiver v2.0.0 (PR #812) renamed the retention setting to ARCHIVER_RETENTION_DAYS with a default of 0; production still set RETENTION_DAYS=30, so the 03:00 run archived and deleted every order. The data is safe in s3://shopsphere-archive/orders/archive_2026-10-22.parquet and can be restored.
